comments.body:
AI generated root cause, that I do agree with:

>  What happens with a validator-thrown ApplicationFailure:                                                                                                                          
>   1. UpdateDispatcher#handleValidateUpdate (UpdateDispatcher.java:65) invokes the user validator; the ApplicationFailure propagates out.
>   2. WorkflowExecutionHandler#handleValidateUpdate (WorkflowExecutionHandler.java:99-110) catches Throwable and calls applyWorkflowFailurePolicyAndRethrow.                         
>   3. applyWorkflowFailurePolicyAndRethrow (WorkflowExecutionHandler.java:136-137) sees e instanceof TemporalFailure, calls throwAndFailWorkflowExecution, which logs a misleading
>   "Workflow execution failure" warning and throws new WorkflowExecutionException(context.mapWorkflowExceptionToFailure(exception)) — a properly-built Failure is attached to the    
>   wrapper.                                                                                                                                                                          
>   4. The generic catch (Exception e) in SyncWorkflow catches the WorkflowExecutionException (it's a RuntimeException) but ignores e.getFailure().                                   
>   5. DefaultFailureConverter#exceptionToFailure (DefaultFailureConverter.java:240-371) walks the type ladder — WorkflowExecutionException matches none of TemporalFailure,          
>   ApplicationFailure, etc. — and falls into the unrecognized-exception branch at line 360-369, synthesizing a fresh ApplicationFailureInfo with type =                              
>   "io.temporal.internal.worker.WorkflowExecutionException" and nonRetryable = false. The original ApplicationFailure (and its Rock type, non-retryable flag, details, message) is   
>   discarded.

title: Update Validator doesn't serialize exceptions properly
